criteria.criterion: A new test in crates/athena-core builds a work tree whose Rust file is mis-formatted (e.g. a long constant on one line), runs the new post-producer format step, and asserts the file is rewritten and `cargo fmt --check` then passes. Run `cargo test -p athena-core` and it passes.
criteria.evidence: `a_misformatted_rust_file_is_rewritten_and_cargo_fmt_check_then_passes` writes a temp crate whose src/lib.rs has a 24-element `pub const TABLE` on one line plus `fn f( )->u32{1}`. It asserts the fmt check fails first, then that `format_work_tree` returns Done, that the file now has rustfmt layout, and that the real `cargo fmt --all --check` passes. I ran it by name and it passed. The full `cargo test -p athena-core -q` gave 1178 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored; the ignored test is not one of the 7 new ones, which all ran and passed by name. Athena's fails-without-1 run shows the tests do not compile once the fix is reverted.

criteria.criterion: A new test shows a fmt failure the formatter cannot fix (e.g. a file that does not parse) still yields a failed fmt result whose output text appears in the failed-check output. Run `cargo test -p athena-core`.
criteria.evidence: `an_unfixable_fmt_error_is_reported_and_the_fmt_check_fails_with_the_same_text` uses `pub fn broken( {`. It asserts the step returns `Unfixed`, that the output has an `error` line, that the file is byte-identical afterwards, and that the configured `cargo fmt --all --check` fails with that same line in its output_tail. It passed in both runs.

criteria.criterion: Grep of crates/athena-core/src/run shows the format step is called after the producer loop and before the checks and verifier run, so the check and the verifier see the formatted tree.
criteria.evidence: I grepped crates/athena-core/src/run. `format_stage` is called once, at producer.rs:406. That is inside each pass of producer_loop, after the report parse (393-403) and before `snapshot.change_list()` (413), `loop_replay` (444) and the loop's break. producer_loop returns to produce_and_verify (mod.rs:1772), which then runs `candidate_stage` (1789) and `check_and_verify` (1814). The end-to-end test that uses the real `cargo fmt --all --check` as the job's check reaches Landed, so the check saw the formatted tree.

criteria.criterion: A test asserts the recorded candidate diff (change list) includes the formatter's changes, not only the producer's own edits. Run `cargo test -p athena-core`.
criteria.evidence: The end-to-end test loads the stored candidate record. It asserts the changes are exactly README.md and src/lib.rs, that `show_file(candidate_commit, "src/lib.rs")` equals TWO_FNS_FORMATTED rather than the producer's mis-formatted text, and that a `format` UI line was printed. `paths_added_by_format_names_only_new_paths` covers the helper. Both passed.

criteria.criterion: The format step runs only for a work tree with a Cargo.toml and is Athena code, not an agent command, so the policy in crates/athena-agent/src/policy.rs that denies `cargo fmt` without --check to agent roles is unchanged.
criteria.evidence: format.rs returns Skipped when there is no Cargo.toml or no changed, non-deleted .rs file, and format_stage also checks for Cargo.toml. The step runs only through `checks::run_check` from host code. `git diff HEAD~1 -- crates/athena-agent ...` is empty, so policy.rs is unchanged, and the stat lists only the five deliverables. The `a_work_tree_without_cargo_toml...` test passed, and `cargo test -p athena-agent -q` gave 65 passed, 2 ignored.

findings.summary: Work kept from a timed-out producer turn is made into a candidate without the format step.
findings.evidence: In producer_loop, the TimedOut branch (producer.rs:372-376) calls keep_timed_out_work before format_stage runs. keep_timed_out_work (mod.rs:938) then calls build_candidate on the unformatted tree. If a later resume (mod.rs:829) sends that candidate straight to check_and_verify without another producer pass, it would reach the fmt check unformatted. I did not trace whether timed-out candidates are resumed that way. Calling format_stage before keep_timed_out_work would close this gap.

findings.summary: The Cargo.toml guard is checked twice.
findings.evidence: format_stage checks `snapshot.dir().join("Cargo.toml").is_file()`, and format_work_tree repeats the same check. This is harmless; the outer check only avoids building the env.

summary: The change does what the reading asked, and every criterion is met: verdict pass. After each producer pass, Athena now runs `cargo fmt --all` and then `cargo fmt --all --check` on the work tree, through `run_check`, before the change list is taken. So the replay, the candidate, the checks and the verifier all see the formatted tree. I ran all seven new tests by name and they passed. They show a mis-formatted file being rewritten until the check passes, a file that does not parse being left alone so the fmt check still fails with the same error text, the recorded candidate holding the formatter's bytes, a run with no Cargo.toml or no changed Rust file being skipped, and the kill switch ending the job at this step before any check or verifier runs. The full athena-core suite passed (1178 passed, 1 ignored), as did athena-agent (65 passed, 2 ignored). Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and test checks passed. The agent policy is unchanged, the dropped job's files are absent, and only the five deliverables changed. One minor gap: work kept after a producer timeout becomes a candidate without being formatted. I did not trace whether such a candidate can reach the checks unformatted through a resume.
